samples.title: Magnitude order: Proof strip
samples.statement:
A technician sorts signed gauge errors by how far they lie from the center mark. Ivo rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

Sort readings by absolute value ascending, breaking ties by numeric value ascending. Keep duplicate readings.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement magnitudeOrderProofStrip(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

samples.title: Magnitude order: Floor ticket
samples.statement:
A technician sorts signed gauge errors by how far they lie from the center mark. Tomas is checking the lower stop before the ribbon press opens. A negative reading is a real measurement and must not be replaced by an invented zero.

Sort readings by absolute value ascending, breaking ties by numeric value ascending. Keep duplicate readings.

Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement magnitudeOrderFloorTicket(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

samples.title: Magnitude order: Boss receipt
samples.statement:
A technician sorts signed gauge errors by how far they lie from the center mark. Sol adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

Sort readings by absolute value ascending, breaking ties by numeric value ascending. Keep duplicate readings.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement magnitudeOrderBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
